problem_markdown: In acute triangle $ABC$, the angle bisector from $A$ meets $BC$ at $L$ and the circumcircle again at $N$. Let $K,M$ be the feet from $L$ to $AB,AC$. Prove quadrilateral $AKNM$ has the same area as $ABC$.
solutions_markdown:
Set $\angle A=2\alpha$. The equal right triangles $AKL,AML$ give $KM\perp AN$. Also $AK=AL\cos\alpha$, so
$$KM=2AK\sin\alpha=AL\sin2\alpha.$$
Thus the quadrilateral has area $AN\cdot KM/2$.

Triangles $ABL$ and $ANC$ are similar: their angles at $A$ agree, and $\angle ABL=\angle ANC$ by the inscribed-angle theorem. Therefore $AB\cdot AC=AL\cdot AN$. Consequently
$$[ABC]=\tfrac12 AB\cdot AC\sin2\alpha=\tfrac12 AN\cdot AL\sin2\alpha=\tfrac12 AN\cdot KM=[AKNM].$$
